# Lyrīon Ltd Portfolio — Master Compliance & Tax Calendar
### Verified: 2026-07-21 | Prepared by Margaret Osei, Head of Finance & Accounting

---

## Part 1 — Verified Rates & Thresholds (July 2026)

### Corporation Tax

The structure introduced on 1 April 2023 continues: **19% small profits rate** up to £50,000, **25% main rate** above £250,000, and marginal relief tapering the effective rate in between.
 
As of today, no changes to corporation tax rates or thresholds have been announced for 2026; the rates introduced from 1 April 2023 continue to apply in full.


> ⚠️ **Multi-entity trap:** 
Thresholds are divided by the number of associated companies plus one.
 Lyrīon Ltd and RenviaIT Ltd are almost certainly **associated companies** under HMRC rules. This means the £50,000 small profits threshold is **halved to £25,000 per entity**. Q must confirm this with a tax adviser — if both companies are associated, any entity making profits above £25,000 enters marginal relief territory early.

### VAT

The VAT registration threshold remains at **£90,000** for the 2025/26 and 2026/27 tax years.
 
You must register within 30 days of crossing it on a rolling 12-month basis, or immediately if you expect to exceed £90,000 in the next 30 days.
 
The deregistration threshold is £88,000.


> ⚠️ **Multi-entity trap:** 
It is a common misconception that each separate business activity gets its own £90,000 allowance. HMRC assesses your total personal business turnover as a whole
 — this applies to sole traders/individuals, but each limited company has its own threshold. SetPostGo runs **under Lyrīon Ltd**, not as a separate company; both revenue streams count toward **one** VAT threshold for Lyrīon Ltd. RenviaIT Ltd is separate.

### Confirmation Statement Fee

As of 1 February 2026, the confirmation statement fee is **£50 when filed online** and £110 for a paper form.


### Making Tax Digital — Income Tax (MTD ITSA)

Those with annual gross income of more than **£50,000** must follow the new Making Tax Digital rules from April 2026.
 
The threshold drops to **£30,000** gross for the 2025/26 tax year (mandated from April 2027) and to **£20,000** for 2026/27 (mandated from April 2028).
 This applies to Q **personally** as a sole trader or director drawing income — not to the companies themselves.

**Priya Raman / Head of SEO & Content — Midday Shift 2026-07-21**

## 1. Strategic Context


Programmatic SEO is the practice of using automation, templates, and structured data to generate hundreds or thousands of optimised landing pages targeting specific, often long-tail keywords.
 SetPostGo is structurally built for this — its product is literally a grid: **professions × platforms × post volume**. That grid IS the keyword universe. We just need to architect it properly.


Programmatic SEO actually favours startups because it rewards systematic thinking over large content teams. A single marketer with the right tools can create and manage thousands of pages. The key is finding underserved keyword patterns that larger competitors haven't addressed.


**The SetPostGo Opportunity in Numbers:**
- 89 professions × 6 platforms = **534 core profession-platform pages**

# Lyrīon Portfolio — UK Compliance Master Calendar 2026/27
### *Verified: 2026-07-21 | Margaret Osei, Head of Finance & Accounting*

> *This document is the institutional compliance backbone for Lyrīon Ltd, RenviaIT Ltd, and NAGORI (nagori.xyz under Lyrīon Ltd). It is a living record — update it every quarter. The ledger never lies, and neither does the Companies House register.*

---

## Part 1: The Regulatory Landscape — What Has Changed in 2026

Three material changes verified this month that every founder must know:

### 1.1 Companies House Confirmation Statement Fee: Now £50

As of 1 February 2026, the confirmation statement fee is **£50** when filed online and **£110** for a paper form.
 This is up from £34. Budget accordingly — with two active entities filing separately (Lyrīon Ltd and RenviaIT Ltd), that is **£100 in mandatory annual filing fees** at minimum.

### 1.2 ECCTA Identity Verification — Hard Deadline: 18 November 2026
This is the most urgent compliance event in the estate. 
Companies House identity verification is the legal requirement, introduced under the Economic Crime and Corporate Transparency Act (ECCTA), for company directors and Persons with Significant Control to confirm their identity. From 18 November 2025, it became mandatory for every new director and new incorporation. **Existing directors and PSCs must verify by 18 November 2026.**


The practical trigger is **earlier** than the headline date: 
existing directors verify by their company's next confirmation statement after the window opens; existing PSCs verify within a set period of a direction from Companies House, or in their birth month, depending on their circumstances.



If you are still putting it off in mid-2026, you are running out of road: existing directors must complete verification by the date of their next annual confirmation statement, and the 12-month transition window closes in November 2026.


**Consequences of non-compliance are severe:** 
Non-compliance constitutes a criminal offence carrying unlimited fines and potential imprisonment. Directors face possible disqualification proceedings, whilst companies cannot incorporate, appoint new directors, or file statutory documents without verified individuals. Perhaps most damaging of all, unverified directors will be permanently marked on the publicly accessible Companies House register — a mark that could undermine business relationships, banking arrangements, and customer confidence for years to come.


**How to verify (free, ~10–20 minutes):** 
The first option is directly through GOV.UK One Login, which asks you to confirm your identity using a passport or driving licence. The quickest method uses the GOV.UK ID Checking App, which takes under three minutes on average.


### 1.3 CT600 Joint Filing Service: Closed Since 1 April 2026

From 1 April 2026, you will need to use commercial software for Company Tax Returns, while annual accounts will still need to be filed separately with Companies House.
 The old HMRC/Companies House joint online service is gone. Q must ensure Lyrīon Ltd and RenviaIT Ltd
